questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the electoral college for the election of the President of India:
1. Elected members of the Legislative Councils of States are not part of it.
2. Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are part of it.
3. Elected members of the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi are part of it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 54 limits the college to elected members of Parliament and State Assemblies; nominated MPs and MLCs are left out because they are not directly elected. The 70th Amendment (1992) added the elected members of the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 54)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the impeachment of the President:
1. It can be initiated only on the ground of violation of the Constitution.
2. The resolution must be passed by two-thirds of the members present and voting in the House.
3. Nominated members of Parliament can participate in the process.
4. Either House of Parliament may prefer the charge.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 61 the resolution needs two-thirds of the TOTAL membership of the House, not of members present and voting, so statement 2 is wrong. Nominated MPs take part in impeachment even though they cannot vote in the election; the charge may start in either House.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 61)
questions.h: Impeachment = 2/3 of the whole House, never of those present.

questions.q: Which one of the following powers is available to the President of India but NOT to a Governor?
o: Power to commute a death sentence passed under a State law
Power to grant a reprieve to a person convicted under a State law
Power to remit the sentence of a person convicted by a State court
Power to pardon a sentence inflicted by a court martial
questions.e: The Governor's clemency power under Article 161 covers only matters within State executive power, so it cannot reach court-martial sentences, which are Union military matters. The President alone can pardon those (Article 72), and also pardons death sentences, which a Governor can only suspend, remit or commute.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 72 vs Art 161)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the ordinance-making power of the President:
1. An ordinance must be laid before Parliament when it reassembles.
2. An ordinance ceases to operate six weeks after Parliament reassembles, unless disapproved earlier by resolutions of both Houses.
3. The President can withdraw an ordinance at any time.
4. An ordinance can be promulgated to amend the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 123 gives an ordinance the same force as an Act, so it can cover only subjects on which Parliament may legislate. A constitutional amendment can be made only under Article 368 by Parliament, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 123)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President of India:
1. He is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members.
2. Members of State Legislative Assemblies take part in his election.
3. He draws a separate salary for the office of Vice-President in addition to the allowances of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Vice-President's college is Parliament alone (Article 66), so State legislators have no role. He has no separate salary as Vice-President; he is paid only as ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and draws the President's emoluments when acting as President.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Vice-President

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Vice-President:
1. The Lok Sabha must agree to the Rajya Sabha resolution by a special majority.
2. The Rajya Sabha resolution must be passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.
3. A notice of at least 14 days is required before the resolution is moved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 67(b) requires an effective majority (majority of all then members) in the Rajya Sabha and only an ordinary (simple) majority in the Lok Sabha, so statement 1 is wrong. Unlike the President, the Vice-President can be removed without proving any specific ground, after 14 days' notice.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Vice-President (Art 67)

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Vice-President, while presiding over the Rajya Sabha, votes only when there is an equality of votes.
Statement-II: The Vice-President is not a member of the Rajya Sabha.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 100 gives the Chairman no original vote, only a casting vote in a tie. This follows from Article 64 and 66(2): he presides ex officio and is not a member of either House.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Vice-President (Art 64, 100)

questions.q: Which of the following is true when the Vice-President acts as the President of India?
o: He continues to preside over the Rajya Sabha in addition to discharging the President's functions
The Deputy Chairman presides over the Rajya Sabha during that period
He draws the salary of Vice-President as well as that of the President
He must resign as Vice-President on assuming the functions of the President
questions.e: Under Article 65 he does not perform the Chairman's duties while acting as President, so the Deputy Chairman presides (Article 91). He receives the President's emoluments, not both, and remains Vice-President.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Vice-President (Art 65)

questions.q: Who was the only Chief Justice of India to have acted as the President of India?
questions.e: After the death of Zakir Husain in 1969, and with V. V. Giri resigning as acting President to contest the election, Chief Justice Hidayatullah acted as President under the Presidents (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969. K. Subba Rao is the tempting wrong choice because he contested the 1967 presidential election after leaving the bench.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 65, 70); Presidents (Discharge of Functions) Act 1969
questions.h: Hidayatullah: the Hidden Judge who filled the President's chair.

questions.q:
With reference to the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, consider the following statements:
1. The total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Union Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
2. In a State, the number of ministers including the Chief Minister shall not be less than 12.
3. A member disqualified on the ground of defection is permanently barred from becoming a minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Amendment capped Union and State councils at 15 per cent of the lower House and set a floor of 12 for a State. A defector is barred from ministership only until the end of the term or until re-elected, whichever is earlier (Article 75(1B)), not permanently.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers (Art 75(1A), 75(1B))

questions.q: A person who is not a member of either House of Parliament is appointed a Union minister. For how long can he continue as minister without becoming a member of either House?
o: Until the end of the next session of Parliament
questions.e: Article 75(5) says a minister who is not a member of either House for any period of six consecutive months ceases to be a minister at the end of that period.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers (Art 75(5))

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General for India:
1. He must be a person qualified for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court.
2. He has the right to speak and take part in proceedings of either House, joint sittings and committees of which he is named a member, but not to vote.
3. He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
4. He is not debarred from private legal practice.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four hold. Articles 76 and 88 give him audience in Parliament without a vote; there is no fixed tenure or removal procedure, and he may take private briefs so long as he does not advise against the Government of India.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Attorney General (Art 76, 88)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Article of the Constitution) with List-II (Provision) and select the correct answer:
List-I: A. Article 61  B. Article 74  C. Article 78  D. Article 87
List-II:
1. Special address by the President to Parliament
2. Duty of the Prime Minister to furnish information to the President
3. Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
4. Impeachment of the President
questions.e: Article 61 deals with impeachment, Article 74 with the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, Article 78 with the Prime Minister's duty to communicate Cabinet decisions to the President, and Article 87 with the special address.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President / Prime Minister

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Case : Principle
1. Shamsher Singh v. State of Punjab : The President and the Governor are bound by the advice of their ministers except where the Constitution requires discretion
2. D. C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar : Repeated re-promulgation of ordinances without placing them before the legislature is impermissible
3. Kehar Singh v. Union of India : The President cannot examine the evidence on record while deciding a mercy petition
4. Ram Jawaya Kapur v. State of Punjab : The Constitution adopts a rigid separation of powers
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. In Kehar Singh the Court held that the President may scrutinise the evidence afresh when considering mercy, and in Ram Jawaya Kapur it held that India does not follow separation of powers in its absolute rigidity.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapters on the President and Governor; landmark cases

questions.q:
Statement-I: Cabinet committees are extra-constitutional bodies.
Statement-II: Cabinet committees are of two types, standing and ad hoc.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Constitution mentions only the Council of Ministers and the 'Cabinet' (Article 352); committees arise from the Rules of Business and the Prime Minister's decision. The standing/ad hoc division is true but does not explain why they are extra-constitutional.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Cabinet Committees

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 74 of the Constitution:
1. The 42nd Amendment made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President.
2. The 44th Amendment allows the President to require reconsideration of the advice once, but he must act on the advice tendered after reconsideration.
3. Courts can inquire into the advice tendered by ministers to the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment made the advice binding; the 44th restored a limited presidential check by allowing one reconsideration. Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring what advice, if any, was given.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers (Art 74)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the President's assent to Bills:
1. The President can return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
2. The President must give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill duly passed under Article 368.
3. The Indian President has a qualified veto, as in the United States.
4. If Parliament re-passes a returned non-money Bill, the President may still withhold assent.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A Money Bill cannot be returned, only assented to or withheld. After the 24th Amendment assent to an amendment Bill is obligatory, and a re-passed Bill must be assented to (Article 111). India has no qualified veto; it has absolute, suspensive and pocket vetoes.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 111, 368)

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT appointed by the President of India?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: The Deputy Chairman is elected by the Rajya Sabha from among its own members (Article 89). The other three are appointed by the President under Articles 148, 316 and 324.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Parliament / President

questions.q: Who among the following was elected President of India unopposed?
questions.e: Reddy was elected in 1977 after all other nominations were rejected or withdrawn. Giri (1969), Husain (1967) and Ahmed (1974) each faced a contest.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President

questions.q:
Arrange the following Presidents of India in the order in which they held office (earliest first):
1. K. R. Narayanan
2. R. Venkataraman
3. Shankar Dayal Sharma
4. Giani Zail Singh
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: Zail Singh (1982-87), Venkataraman (1987-92), Sharma (1992-97), Narayanan (1997-2002).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President; list of Presidents

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding nomination of candidates for the election of the President:
1. A nomination must be proposed by at least 50 electors and seconded by at least 50 electors.
2. The security deposit is Rs 15,000.
3. For the election of the Vice-President, the nomination requires 10 proposers and 10 seconders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1997 amendment to the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act raised the requirement to 50 proposers and 50 seconders and the deposit to Rs 15,000, to discourage frivolous candidates. For the Vice-President the numbers are 20 and 20.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President; Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding disputes about the election of the President:
1. All doubts and disputes are decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final.
2. The election cannot be questioned on the ground of any vacancy in the electoral college.
3. If the election is declared void, all acts done by him before the decision become invalid.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 71 protects an incomplete electoral college and says acts done in office before the Supreme Court's decision remain valid; invalidating them would create chaos in governance.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 71)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the election of the President:
1. The voting is by secret ballot.
2. The system is proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
3. The value of an MLA's vote is calculated on the basis of the 2011 Census population of the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 55 prescribes both secret ballot and STV. For vote-value, 'population' is still taken from the 1971 Census, frozen until the first Census after 2026 has been published.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 55)

questions.q: To whom does the President of India address his resignation?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Under Article 56(2) the President resigns by a letter addressed to the Vice-President, who then communicates it to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 56)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding vacancies in the offices of the President and the Vice-President:
1. An election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President caused by death must be held within six months.
2. An election to fill a vacancy in the office of President caused by death must be held within six months.
3. A person elected to fill a casual vacancy holds office for a full term of five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 62 fixes six months for the President, but Article 68 says only 'as soon as possible' for the Vice-President. In both cases the new incumbent serves a fresh five-year term.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President / Vice-President (Art 62, 68)

questions.q: Which one of the following proclamations must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month of its issue, failing which it ceases to operate?
o: Proclamation of President's Rule under Article 356
Proclamation of Financial Emergency under Article 360
Promulgation of an ordinance under Article 123
Proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352
questions.e: The 44th Amendment cut the period for a national emergency from two months to one. Proclamations under Articles 356 and 360 still have two months, and an ordinance has six weeks from reassembly.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Emergency Provisions
questions.h: National = 1 month; the other two proclamations = 2 months.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : Provision
1. Article 63 : There shall be a Vice-President of India
2. Article 65 : Qualifications for election as Vice-President
3. Article 69 : Oath or affirmation by the Vice-President
4. Article 70 : Removal of the Vice-President
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Article 65 deals with the Vice-President acting as President (qualifications are in Article 66(3)), and removal is in Article 67(b); Article 70 is about the discharge of the President's functions in other contingencies.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Vice-President

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Attorney General has the right to speak in the Houses of Parliament.
Statement-II: The Attorney General is a member of Parliament.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 88 gives the Attorney General, like every minister, a right to speak in either House but no right to vote. He need not be a member of Parliament at all, which is why he cannot vote.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Attorney General (Art 88)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Nominated members of Parliament can vote in the election of the Vice-President but not in the election of the President.
Statement-II: The electoral college for the Vice-President consists of all members of Parliament, whereas that for the President consists of elected members of Parliament and of State Legislative Assemblies.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The two colleges are defined differently in Articles 54 and 66, and the Vice-President's college, being 'members of both Houses', includes the 12 nominated Rajya Sabha members and any nominated Lok Sabha members. That is exactly why they vote in one election and not the other.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapters on the President and Vice-President

questions.q:
Statement-I: No civil proceedings of any kind can be instituted against the President during his term of office.
Statement-II: No criminal proceedings can be instituted or continued against the President during his term of office.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 361 gives absolute immunity from criminal proceedings, but civil proceedings for personal acts can be started after two months' written notice. So Statement-I's 'of any kind' is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 361)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding nominated members of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.
2. Nominated members can vote in the election of the President.
3. Nominated members can vote in the election of the Vice-President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 80 the 12 nominees are chosen for special knowledge in literature, science, art and social service. They are excluded from the presidential college (only 'elected' members count) but are part of the Vice-President's college.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Parliament (Art 80, 54, 66)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the responsibility of the Council of Ministers:
1. It is collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
2. It is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
3. A minister who disagrees with a Cabinet decision must either accept it or resign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 75(3) makes the Council collectively responsible to the House of the People alone, which is why only a Lok Sabha defeat brings the government down. Collective responsibility means all ministers stand by one decision.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister:
1. He is the link between the President and the Council of Ministers (Article 78).
2. He must necessarily be a member of the Lok Sabha.
3. The death or resignation of the Prime Minister dissolves the Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Prime Minister may belong to either House, as Indira Gandhi in 1966 and Manmohan Singh in 2004 did from the Rajya Sabha. Since other ministers are appointed on his advice, the Council cannot outlive him.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Prime Minister (Art 75, 78)
questions.h: Keystone of the Cabinet arch: remove him and the arch falls.

questions.q: The collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the House of the People is laid down in which of the following provisions?
questions.e: Article 75(2) says ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President (individual responsibility), while Article 75(3) provides collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 77:
1. All executive action of the Government of India is expressed to be taken in the name of the President.
2. The President makes rules for the more convenient transaction of business and for its allocation among ministers.
3. An order authenticated as prescribed can be challenged on the ground that it was not made by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 77(2) shields an authenticated order from objection on the ground that it was not made by the President personally; this is why the Rules of Business can work through officials.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President / Cabinet (Art 77)

questions.q:
Which of the following can the President of India do in relation to Parliament?
1. Prorogue both Houses
2. Dissolve the Rajya Sabha
3. Dissolve the Lok Sabha
4. Summon a joint sitting of the two Houses
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every second year. The President summons the Houses, prorogues them, dissolves the Lok Sabha (Article 85) and summons joint sittings (Article 108).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President / Parliament (Art 85, 108)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the President's address to Parliament under Article 87:
1. The President addresses both Houses assembled together at the first session after each general election and at the first session of every year.
2. The address is prepared by the Government.
3. The President delivers separate addresses to the two Houses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The address is a joint one and is drafted by the Cabinet, so it states government policy; a Motion of Thanks follows. Failure to pass it would amount to a defeat of the government.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 87)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about oaths is correct?
o: The oath to the President is administered by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The oath to the Prime Minister is administered by the Chief Justice of India
The oath to the Vice-President is administered by the President or a person appointed by him
The oath to the President is administered by the Vice-President
questions.e: The Chief Justice of India (or the senior-most Supreme Court judge) administers the oath to the President (Article 60); the President administers it to the Vice-President and to the Prime Minister and ministers.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapters on the President and Vice-President (Art 60, 69)

questions.q: Under Article 88 of the Constitution, which one of the following is correct?
o: A Union minister who is a member of the Lok Sabha may speak and vote in the Rajya Sabha
A Union minister who is a member of the Lok Sabha may speak in the Rajya Sabha but cannot vote there
A minister who is not a member of either House cannot speak in Parliament
Only a Cabinet minister has the right to speak in the House of which he is not a member
questions.e: Article 88 extends the right to speak and take part in proceedings to every minister and the Attorney General in either House, but the right to vote belongs only to the House of which one is a member.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers (Art 88)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the emoluments of the President:
1. They cannot be diminished during his term of office.
2. They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
3. They are subject to annual vote by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 59(3) protects them during his term and Article 112(3) places them in the charged list, which Parliament may discuss but not vote on, so the President's independence is not at the mercy of the Lok Sabha.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 59, 112)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 143 (advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court):
1. The President may refer a question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court.
2. The Supreme Court is bound to give its opinion on every reference made under Article 143(1).
3. The opinion given by the Supreme Court is binding on the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The word in Article 143(1) is 'may'; in the Ayodhya reference (1993) the Court respectfully declined to answer. The opinion is advisory, not binding.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Supreme Court (Art 143)

questions.q: In practice, how is an individual Union minister removed from the Council of Ministers during the life of the government?
o: The Lok Sabha passes a resolution against him by a special majority
The Council of Ministers collectively resolves to remove him
The Chief Justice of India recommends removal to the President
The President acts on the advice of the Prime Minister
questions.e: Article 75(2) says ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, but the President can dismiss one only on the Prime Minister's advice, as the Prime Minister can ask a minister to resign or advise dismissal.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers (Art 75(2))

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Kitchen Cabinet:
1. It is an informal body of the Prime Minister's most trusted colleagues.
2. It enjoys constitutional status under Article 75.
3. It may include persons from outside the Cabinet whom the Prime Minister trusts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Kitchen or Inner Cabinet is an extra-constitutional device that lets a Prime Minister take quick decisions without the full Cabinet. It exists in practice, not in the Constitution.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Cabinet / Kitchen Cabinet

questions.q: The population base of the 1971 Census was retained for calculating the value of votes in the Presidential election until the first Census after 2026 by which one of the following Amendments?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment froze the base till 2000, and the 84th extended the freeze to the first Census after 2026 in Article 55(3), keeping the value of every vote tied to 1971 population.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 55(3))

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 53 of the Constitution:
1. The executive power of the Union is vested in the President.
2. It can be exercised only by the President personally and not through subordinate officers.
3. The supreme command of the Defence Forces is vested in the President, and its exercise is regulated by law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 53(1) allows exercise either directly or through officers subordinate to him; no President can personally run a government, and the Council of Ministers does so in his name.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 53)

questions.q: A person is NOT regarded as holding an office of profit, and therefore is not disqualified from being a candidate for President, if he is the:
o: Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
questions.e: Article 58(2) names the President, the Vice-President, a Governor and a Union or State minister as offices that do not count as offices of profit.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (Art 58)

questions.q: Which of the following Vice-Presidents of India later became the President of India?
questions.e: Zakir Husain was Vice-President (1962-67) and then President (1967-69). Jatti only acted as President in 1977; Pathak and Ansari never held the office.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Vice-President; list of office-holders

questions.q: Which one of the following Bills was subjected to a pocket veto by the President in 1986?
o: The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Amendment Bill
questions.e: President Zail Singh neither signed nor returned the Bill, since the Constitution gives no time limit for a decision; it lapsed with the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. The 2006 disqualification Bill was returned by President Kalam, a different veto.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the President (pocket veto)
questions.h: Zail Singh left the Post Office Bill sitting in the post box.

questions.q: Which one of the following posts is NOT mentioned in the Constitution of India?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.e: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General are statutory or administrative posts that assist the Attorney General, who is the only law officer named in Article 76.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Attorney General

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Union Council of Ministers and the Cabinet:
1. The Cabinet is a smaller body within the Council of Ministers.
2. The Council of Ministers as a whole meets regularly to take policy decisions.
3. Decisions of the Cabinet are binding on all ministers, including those outside the Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Council (Cabinet ministers, Ministers of State, Deputy Ministers) rarely meets as a body; the Cabinet, the real executive, decides policy and its decisions bind everyone in the Council through collective responsibility.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on the Central Council of Ministers
